subject: SKU reallocation + transition schedule for additional capacity

Subject: Request: add capacity + SKU reallocation (proposed CO attached)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at OliveHealth is ready to proceed with the next phase. We have a short request: we need to add 120k inference units for our clinical OCR workload and reallocate 30% of our existing GPU SKUs toward higher-throughput instances for the remaining term. We attached a proposed change order (OliveHealth_ChangeOrder_20261003.pdf) that lays out the SKU swaps, new throughput numbers, and a proposed effective date of 2026-11-01.

Two asks up front: can Redwood confirm (1) whether pricing will be pro-rated for the newly requested capacity and (2) how this SKU reallocation affects the existing orderform exhibits / billing lines? Procurement is looped (procurement@olivehealth.com).

Appreciate a quick read — we are targeting a sign by Oct 12 to hit engineering timelines.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Cloud Ops
OliveHealth

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the attached change order. I'm Markus (legal) — looping in Karthik (account lead) and Laura (procurement/finance) to confirm commercial and billing impacts.

Quick notes from legal review:
- We'll need a short amendment (change order) referencing your existing Order Form #OH-2025-07 and an updated Exhibit A showing the SKU mapping.
- Please confirm whether OliveHealth expects any SLAs to change (latency/availability) as part of the reallocation — if so, we will need to reflect that in the SLA exhibit.
- For billing, we typically pro-rate for mid-term capacity increases; procurement will confirm the exact proration method.

Laura/Karthik — can you weigh in on pricing/proration approach and whether Redwood can offer a phased migration so they only start paying for migrated SKUs once traffic switches over?

I'll prepare a redline of the Order Form and a short amendment template for signature once we confirm the billing approach.

Regards,

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: add capacity + SKU reallocation (proposed CO attached)

Thanks for the loop. Reading the change order now — preliminary procurement notes:

- Pricing impact: the incremental 120k inference units would be billed at the current tier pricing in their orderform (Exhibit B). If we pro-rate, we calculate charges from the effective date (they asked for 2026-11-01) through the next billing cycle and apply a one-time invoice.
- SKU reallocation: moving 30% of existing SKUs to higher-throughput SKUs will change the per-unit cost for those instances. We need the expected traffic shift percentage and target instance types (they listed a few in the CO but not model/instance mapping).
- Billing lines: we'll create a new line item for the added capacity and mark the reallocated SKUs as 'redistributed' in Exhibit A; this avoids creating new PO lines for the same contractual term.
- Taxes/terms: confirm whether OliveHealth needs a separate purchase order number for the amendment.

Action items for sales/legal to resolve before redline:
1) Sales confirms target effective date and whether phased migration acceptable.
2) Customer confirms whether they want pro-rated billing or to delay billing until cutover.
3) Legal to prepare orderform amendment + Exhibit A redline.

Markus — if you can produce the redline today we can route to procurement and send a single DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Procurement Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@olivehealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: add capacity + SKU reallocation (proposed CO attached)

Elena — appreciate the quick turnaround. To minimize disruption for your team, Redwood can offer a phased SKU migration:

- Phase 1 (2026-11-01): provision incremental 60k units (50% of ask) on new higher-throughput SKUs; billing pro-rated from effective date.
- Phase 2 (2026-12-01): move remaining 60k units and finalize SKU percentages once traffic baselines are validated.

On pricing: we can keep the incremental units at the customer's current tier pricing for the first quarter post-migration as a goodwill concession. After that quarter, normal tiering applies.

Next steps:
- If you are OK with phased approach and the effective dates above, we'll proceed with Marku's redline and send a single DocuSign link for the amendment.
- Please confirm whether OliveHealth requires a PO number for the amendment.

Elena / Procurement team — attaching the redlined Order Form and a short amendment template for signature. Key legal points called out in the redline:

- Amendment references Order Form OH-2025-07 and adds a new Exhibit A (SKU mapping) + Exhibit B (fee schedule update).
- Pro-rated billing language: charges for incremental capacity will be pro-rated from the amendment effective date to the next invoice. We've added a clause to clarify credits if traffic does not cut over within 45 days.
- SLA: no change to availability SLA; latency commitments remain as-is. If OliveHealth wants to add specific latency targets for the new SKU types, we'll need a separate SLA exhibit (we flagged this in the redline).
- Signature flow: we propose one DocuSign envelope for the amendment + redlined Exhibit A. Karthik, please include the agreed phased dates and PO number in the envelope.
